key_insight: A finite-volume convolution unit (FVCU) lets CNN super-resolution work directly on non-uniform, non-orthogonal meshes by building convolutions from finite-volume operators instead of assuming a uniform grid.
engineering_relevance: This makes data-driven turbulence reconstruction usable on the kinds of meshes actually used in wall-bounded and complex-geometry CFD, bridging ML super-resolution and practical engineering simulations.
method: Replace standard CNN convolutions with a finite-volume convolution unit (FVCU).
Decompose 3D convolution into successive axis-wise operations using gradient, averaging, and identity operators that are valid on arbitrary polyhedral cells.
Condition the network with a Van Driest damping input to encode wall proximity.
evidence_signal: The model was trained and tested on 4× coarsened channel-flow and circular-pipe-flow data, and it reproduced instantaneous velocity fields, Reynolds stresses, anisotropy, and spectra beyond the low-resolution Nyquist limit; on an unseen elliptic pipe it recovered the main flow features with only modest small-scale energy overprediction.
watch_item: Performance on unseen geometries is promising but still shows some small-scale spectral bias, so generalization to more complex meshes and flows should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Extending convolutional neural networks to finite-volume meshes for fine-scale reconstruction of wall-bounded turbulence
